claims.statement: For user interface components, name and role are programmatically determinable; user-settable states, properties, and values are programmatically settable; change notification is available to user agents including assistive technologies.
exclusions: does not prescribe one universal widget implementation

claims.statement: When a control has a visible text label, its accessible name contains that text subject to the Success Criterion exceptions.
exclusions: does not require every accessible name to be visible

claims.statement: When sequential navigation order affects meaning or operation, focusable components receive focus in an order that preserves meaning and operability.
exclusions: does not prescribe DOM order as the only implementation

claims.statement: Text and images of text meet the WCAG 2.2 minimum contrast ratios subject to the stated large-text, incidental, and logotype exceptions.
exclusions: does not apply the normal-text ratio to exempt content

claims.statement: Visual information needed to identify user interface components and states meets the WCAG 2.2 non-text contrast criterion subject to its exceptions.
exclusions: does not treat inactive components as in-scope when the criterion excludes them

claims.statement: Except for captions and images of text, text can be resized up to 200 percent without loss of content or functionality.
exclusions: does not claim that browser zoom and text-only resize are identical mechanisms

claims.statement: Ordinary content can be presented without loss of information or functionality and without two-dimensional scrolling at the criterion's stated dimensions, except for content requiring two-dimensional layout for usage or meaning.
exclusions: preserves the two-dimensional-layout exception

claims.statement: A custom control exposes an applicable non-abstract WAI-ARIA role with the semantics and required properties defined for that role.
claims.scope: WAI-ARIA 1.2 role model and role definitions
exclusions: does not use abstract roles
does not override conflicting strong native semantics

claims.statement: Applicable WAI-ARIA states and properties expose the current control state or value according to their defined semantics and allowed values.
exclusions: does not invent a property unsupported by the chosen role

claims.statement: Accessible names are computed from referenced author labels, aria-label, host-language labeling, or name-from-content according to the normative precedence algorithm.
claims.scope: Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.1 section 4.3
exclusions: does not treat placeholder or visual position as a stable label without a conforming name source

claims.statement: Identify dependency failure modes and place an explicit isolation or degradation boundary so the failure affects only a limited component set while the component preserves its critical function where possible.
exclusions: does not prescribe cells for every workload
does not claim every dependency can be softened

claims.statement: Set a realistic caller deadline and, when a server makes downstream RPCs for that call, propagate the original deadline as a timeout with elapsed time deducted so downstream work cannot outlive the caller's budget.
claims.scope: gRPC Deadlines guide, Deadlines on the Client and Deadline Propagation
exclusions: does not prescribe one numeric timeout for all calls
does not claim every transport propagates deadlines automatically

claims.statement: Before automatic retries, verify the service operation is idempotent; bound retries by a maximum attempt count or elapsed-time limit and choose timeouts and stop conditions for the use case.
exclusions: does not make a non-idempotent operation safe by adding backoff
does not prescribe one universal attempt count

claims.statement: A circuit breaker monitors downstream call failures, stops sending requests when failures are sufficiently high, and later admits limited probes to test whether the downstream system recovered.
claims.scope: AWS Well-Architected REL05-BP01, Implementation steps item 2
exclusions: does not open solely because one caller is unwilling to wait
does not prescribe one universal failure threshold or probe interval

claims.statement: Define RTO from acceptable service-restoration delay and RPO from acceptable data loss, then select a recovery, replication, standby, or active-active strategy that can meet those objectives within explicit cost and complexity constraints.
exclusions: does not claim active-active is universally preferable
does not equate replication alone with protection from corruption

claims.statement: Recovery evidence must include controlled component-loss or failover exercises and restored-data validation that checks availability, accessibility, and corruption, rather than proving only that a host can be replaced.
exclusions: does not authorize unguarded production fault injection
does not treat backup existence as proof of recoverability

claims.statement: When not all work can be served, identify the component's core business function and preserve its most critical functionality while degrading or dropping less critical work according to explicit business requirements.
exclusions: does not infer request value without a stated business criticality
does not permit dropping correctness requirements that define the core function

claims.statement: When overload or a dependency failure prevents normal work, return an explicit throttling, failure, or partial-result indication that the caller can handle; do not present silently omitted work as a normal complete result.
exclusions: does not require one universal HTTP status for non-HTTP protocols
does not claim every optional field must be returned during degradation

claims.statement: All functionality is operable through a keyboard interface without individual-keystroke timing requirements, except where the underlying function depends on the path of movement.
exclusions: Does not require every pointer control to have a one-to-one keyboard control when equivalent functionality is available.
Preserves the path-dependent-function exception.

claims.statement: Web content does not restrict input modalities available on the platform except where essential, required for security, or required to respect user settings.
exclusions: Preserves the essential, security, and user-setting exceptions.

claims.statement: Color is not the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element.
exclusions: Does not prohibit using color as an additional cue.

claims.statement: When an input error is automatically detected, the item in error is identified and the error is described to the user in text.
exclusions: Does not itself require a correction suggestion when one is unknown.

claims.statement: Information, structure, and relationships conveyed through presentation are programmatically determinable or available in text.
exclusions: Does not mandate one particular association attribute.

claims.statement: When a host-language feature with identical role semantics and values is available and there is no compelling reason to avoid it, authors should use the host-language feature instead of repurposing another element with WAI-ARIA.
exclusions: Does not claim a native control is sufficient when its semantics or values do not match the required interaction.

claims.statement: aria-errormessage identifies the element containing an object's error message and is used with aria-invalid when that message is pertinent.
exclusions: Does not claim aria-errormessage is supported on a role that does not permit it.
Does not replace the requirement that the error be available as visible text when WCAG 3.3.1 applies.

claims.statement: The accessibility of interactive content cannot be confirmed by static checks alone.
exclusions: Does not prescribe one browser, assistive technology, or automated tool matrix.
Does not establish a performance-testing claim.

claims.statement: Developers of interactive content should test device-independent access and verify accessibility API access to all content and changes during user interaction.
exclusions: Does not prove a specific screen reader and browser combination without observed evidence.

claims.statement: Isolate domain-model expression and business logic from UI, persistence, application, and infrastructure concerns so domain objects do not display or store themselves.
exclusions: does not by itself identify commands or queries
does not prescribe a framework

claims.statement: Model an object as an entity when identity and lifecycle continuity distinguish it even while attributes or representations change.
exclusions: does not equate persistence-generated keys with domain identity in every model

claims.statement: Model a concept as a value object when only attributes and related logic matter; give it no identity and treat it as immutable with side-effect-free operations.
exclusions: does not apply when independent identity or lifecycle continuity is required

claims.statement: An entity is responsible for tracking its state and the rules regulating its lifecycle.
exclusions: does not move unrelated application orchestration or persistence behavior into the entity

claims.statement: Define aggregate-wide properties and invariants, assign enforcement to the aggregate root or designated mechanism, use the same aggregate boundary for transactions, enforce within it synchronously, and handle cross-boundary updates asynchronously.
exclusions: does not authorize temporary invariant violation inside the aggregate
does not claim all related objects belong to one aggregate

claims.statement: A repository offers domain-meaningful selection and returns fully instantiated domain objects, collections, or aggregate proxies while encapsulating storage and query technology.
exclusions: does not expose database query mechanics to domain callers
does not require a repository for every type

claims.statement: A downstream system can protect its own domain model by placing an isolating layer at the upstream boundary that translates between the upstream and downstream models.
exclusions: does not make upstream names, types, or error semantics part of the downstream domain model

claims.statement: For protobuf integrations whose clients and servers roll out independently, do not reuse tag numbers or casually change field types; reserve deleted numbers and names to preserve stored and in-flight compatibility.
exclusions: does not generalize to every serialization format
does not make provider field names domain vocabulary

claims.statement: For HTTP Problem Details, consumers use the type URI as the primary problem identifier; problem details expose the HTTP interface, not underlying implementation or a replacement for an existing domain-specific error format.
exclusions: does not make a provider problem type a core-domain failure type
does not authorize exposing implementation internals

claims.statement: Automatic HTTP retry depends on idempotent request semantics, and Retry-After explicitly communicates when a follow-up request ought to occur.
claims.scope: RFC 9110 HTTP retry and idempotency semantics
exclusions: does not imply every provider error is retryable
does not define domain recovery policy

claims.statement: For a Google-style API operation that supports request identification, a client-provided request_id uniquely identifies the request; when it is provided, duplicate delivery is detected, the operation is processed only once, and the prior successful response is normally returned during the documented honoring window.
claims.scope: Google AIP-155 request identification and idempotency guidance
exclusions: does not claim every API or transport implements request_id
does not claim the honoring window is infinite
allows the documented stale-success exception to return current resource state

claims.statement: For Google-style unary RPCs, automatic retry is permitted only when repetition cannot cause unintended state changes and the status semantics are retryable; other statuses require surfacing the failure or waiting for the stated repair condition, such as authentication, permission, resource creation, or system-state change.
exclusions: does not cover client-streaming or bidirectional-streaming RPCs
does not make all transient-looking failures retryable
does not replace transaction-level retry logic

claims.statement: For a mutating operation selected for idempotency, the sender supplies a unique token; the service stores the token with operation state and response, checks it before execution, and returns the stored or previous result for a completed duplicate instead of executing the mutation again.
claims.scope: AWS Well-Architected REL04-BP04 idempotent mutating operations
exclusions: does not apply idempotency indiscriminately to every operation
does not prescribe one storage product or infinite retention window
does not treat timestamps or whole mutable payloads as universally safe idempotency keys

claims.statement: Within the same major Google API version, components may be added only while old clients continue to work and receive the prior treatment: no new required request/resource fields, client-populated fields preserve prior default behavior, server-populated fields remain populated, and visible semantics are not changed in a way likely to break reasonable client code.
claims.scope: Google AIP-180 adding components and semantic compatibility
exclusions: does not claim every additive syntax change is semantically compatible
does not authorize removal, rename, type change, or changed default behavior
is scoped to the AIP's protobuf/JSON and Google-style API assumptions

claims.statement: Do not grant trust from network location alone. For a protected resource request, validate the subject and request, obtain an authentication and authorization decision before access, and enforce that decision at a policy enforcement point that gates the communication path to the resource.
claims.scope: NIST SP 800-207 zero-trust access model, tenets, and PEP
exclusions: does not prescribe one universal API-gateway product or topology
does not claim one initial login validates every later resource request
does not apply the enterprise-resource model to anonymous public access

claims.statement: Authorize a requested operation on each protected object from current subject, object/resource, operation, and relevant environment attributes; authorization to one resource does not automatically grant access to another. Tenant ownership may be an object/resource attribute only when it is authoritatively assigned and enforced by policy.
claims.scope: NIST SP 800-207 individual-resource access and NIST SP 800-162 ABAC
exclusions: does not treat caller-supplied tenant text as authoritative
does not prescribe a tenant storage layout or query implementation
does not replace authentication with authorization attributes

claims.statement: For online guessing against an authenticator, the verifier rate-limits consecutive failed attempts for the specific authenticator on the single subscriber account and disables the affected authenticator when the configured upper bound is reached.
exclusions: does not generalize the 100-attempt upper bound to other abuse vectors
does not prescribe IP-only throttling
does not ignore legitimate-user lockout risk

claims.statement: Propagate a trace context containing TraceId and SpanId across process boundaries; include those identifiers in request-processing log records and in metric exemplars where a metric event is linked to a trace, so telemetry for one request and its component spans can be correlated across logs, traces, and metrics.
claims.scope: OpenTelemetry Specification 1.60.0 trace context, log correlation, and metric exemplars
exclusions: does not require every log record or metric point to carry trace context
does not claim correlation proves causation
does not use user identity or secrets as telemetry correlation identifiers

claims.statement: To remove a protobuf enum name used for interchange, first add the new alias after the old name and deprecate the old one; after every parser has the schema, swap alias order so writers emit the new name while readers accept both; delete the deprecated name only after every serializer has the later schema.
exclusions: does not generalize this exact sequence to arbitrary database migrations
does not permit deleting the old name before both parser and serializer rollout gates
does not authorize reuse of deleted enum numbers

claims.statement: Authorization rules are enforced at a trusted service layer and do not rely on client-side controls that an untrusted consumer can manipulate.
claims.scope: Web application authorization decisions where browser presentation state is not a trusted enforcement boundary.
exclusions: Does not establish where every non-authorization computation must run.
Does not claim that hiding a control is unnecessary as a presentation choice.

claims.statement: Function-level and data-specific access are restricted to consumers with explicit permission for the function and requested data item.
claims.scope: Server-side authorization of a requested action and resource for the authenticated or otherwise identified consumer.
exclusions: Does not select RBAC, ABAC, or another authorization model.
Does not prove the freshness of client-cached permission presentation.

claims.statement: Changes to values used for authorization are applied immediately; if that cannot be done, mitigating controls alert on a now-unauthorized action and revert it.
claims.scope: Authorization inputs that can change while a client or self-contained authorization representation remains stale.
exclusions: The stated mitigation does not prevent information leakage.
Does not prescribe a particular client cache invalidation mechanism.

claims.statement: Sensitive data is identified and classified, and controls for retention, logging, privacy, and confidentiality are documented and implemented for its protection level.
claims.scope: Application-defined sensitive data and the storage, telemetry, and retention controls derived from its classified protection level.
exclusions: Does not decide which non-sensitive data is necessary for a product feature.
Does not replace applicable privacy law or a qualified legal assessment.

claims.statement: The application returns only the minimum sensitive data required for the application functionality.
claims.scope: Sensitive results returned to a browser or other client for the stated user functionality.
exclusions: Does not require minimising non-sensitive response fields.
Does not authorize returning a full sensitive value merely because the client can hide it.

claims.statement: Browser storage such as localStorage, sessionStorage, IndexedDB, or cookies does not contain sensitive data, except session tokens under their separate security contract.
claims.scope: Application data written to browser-managed storage.
exclusions: Does not declare session tokens safe without the separate session-management and cookie controls.
Does not define browser quota or eviction behavior.

claims.statement: Personal data used for telemetry is tied to a specified purpose and limited to what is necessary; appropriate technical measures such as pseudonymisation are considered to implement data minimisation by design.
claims.scope: Telemetry containing personal data in a GDPR-applicable teaching case with a stated diagnostic purpose.
exclusions: Does not apply GDPR to anonymous or out-of-scope data by assertion.
Pseudonymised data remains personal data when it can be attributed using additional information.
Does not supply jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

claims.statement: Identifiable personal data is kept no longer than necessary for the purposes for which it is processed, subject to the regulation's stated archival, research, statistical, and safeguard conditions.
claims.scope: Retention of personal data in a GDPR-applicable teaching case with a specified diagnostic purpose.
exclusions: Does not set a universal numeric retention period.
Does not erase the regulation's stated longer-retention conditions.
Does not supply jurisdiction-specific legal advice.

claims.statement: An invariant-bearing class establishes its invariant during construction, does not leave an invalid constructed object, and requires public member functions to reestablish the invariant on exit.
claims.scope: C++ Core Guidelines C.2, C.40, C.41, and C.42 at the pinned commit
exclusions: Does not prescribe one validation library or exception type.
Does not prove invariants spanning multiple independently owned objects.
Does not authorize delayed validation after invalid state is observable.

claims.statement: Concurrent unsynchronized access to the same object is a data race when at least one access writes; an interleaving can therefore lose updates or expose an impossible value.
claims.scope: C++ Core Guidelines CP.2 definition and examples
exclusions: Does not identify a race without concrete shared-object, access, and synchronization evidence.
Does not select a lock, actor, transaction, or message-passing implementation.

claims.statement: Immutable data can be shared without locking, while passing a small value by value gives unique ownership and can cost less than coordinating shared writable state.
claims.scope: C++ Core Guidelines CP.3 and CP.31 conditional tradeoff
exclusions: Does not claim copying is cheaper for large values.
Does not require immutability when mutation ownership or copying cost makes synchronization the safer boundary.
Does not generalize C++ constness into deep immutability without model evidence.

claims.statement: Mutable data that requires synchronization should be defined together with the mutex that guards it so the required lock and guarded state have one evident ownership boundary.
exclusions: Does not claim one mutex is sufficient for every compound cross-object invariant.
Does not select lock granularity without the concrete access pattern.

claims.statement: A resource handle tied to lexical/object scope pairs acquisition with release so cleanup occurs on normal completion and exceptional or abrupt exit.
claims.scope: C++ Core Guidelines R.1 plus Java SE 25 JLS 14.20.3
exclusions: Does not make a cleanup operation infallible.
Does not define retry policy or a remote-resource compensation protocol.
Language-specific RAII and try-with-resources mechanics must not be presented as identical syntax.

claims.statement: In Java try-with-resources, resources initialize left to right; if a later initialization throws, every resource initialized so far is automatically closed before the statement propagates the failure.
exclusions: Does not expose a partially initialized resource as a successful handle.
Does not define safe retry or idempotent initialization.
Does not generalize automatic cleanup to resources outside the declared resource specification.

claims.statement: A UML Message with an Operation signature binds request arguments to in/inout parameters and reply arguments to out/inout/return parameters; the Operation also owns preconditions, postconditions, and the Types of exceptions that may be raised.
exclusions: Does not prescribe transport serialization, timeout, retry, or delivery semantics.
Does not treat internal collaborator fields as message inputs.
Does not claim UML raisedException types define a product-specific domain failure taxonomy.
